mainTopic: חזקיהו's prayer and the merit of others, rules of תפלה, the deadline for the morning שמע, and posture during שמע
overview: This amud finishes the story of חזקיהו's illness and prayer. רבי חנן teaches that even if a dream says you will die, you should keep praying, and חזקיהו turned 'to the wall' and prayed. ריש לקיש explains 'wall' as the walls of his heart, and רבי לוי reads it as a merit from the שונמית's small wall for אלישע. A ברייתא then lists six deeds of חזקיהו: the חכמים approved three and disapproved three. One of the disapproved deeds, a leap year declared on the 30th of אדר, is explained through a rule of שמואל. רבי יוחנן teaches that whoever asks in his own merit is answered through others' merit, and the reverse, using משה and חזקיהו as examples. The גמרא then explains the שונמית's room and how she recognized אלישע's holiness. It brings rules for תפלה: pray from a low place, keep your feet together, and do not eat before praying. Back in the משנה, the הלכה follows רבי יהושע that the morning שמע may be said until three hours, and a late reader still says the ברכות. A new משנה brings the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל about body position during שמע, with the story of רבי טרפון.

steps.title: Even a dream of death should not stop a person from praying
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנן teaches that even if a dream tells a person he will die tomorrow, he should still pray for רחמים. He brings a פסוק from קהלת as his source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנן said: Even if the master of dreams tells a person, 'Tomorrow you will die,' he should not hold himself back from praying for mercy. As the פסוק says: 'For in the many dreams and vanities there are many words; but fear God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching from רבי חנן that matches חזקיהו's message: never stop praying, even when it looks like the end has been decreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a 'master of dreams' (a dream that feels true, or even an angel in a dream) does not have the final word. The פסוק says dreams carry 'many words' and vanities, but what matters is to 'fear God,' meaning to turn to Him. So the dream's message is not a reason to stop praying.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'master of dreams' — a dream that feels real, or the angel in charge of dreams
Mercy; here it means praying to ה׳ for mercy
He should not hold himself back
As it is said — introduces a פסוק as a source

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle in תפילה: no situation is so hopeless that praying is pointless.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a dream predicting death should not stop a person from praying for mercy.

steps.title: חזקיהו turns to the wall and prays
steps.stepSummary: The story goes on: right away, חזקיהו turned his face to the wall and prayed to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately, 'חזקיהו turned his face to the wall and prayed to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the story and quotes the פסוק in ישעיהו showing that חזקיהו acted on his belief and prayed right away. This sets up the next question about the word 'wall.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'immediately' (מיד) shows that חזקיהו did exactly what he had just taught: he did not give up, and he turned to תפילה at once. The odd detail that he faced 'the wall' is what the גמרא will now ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately
And he turned
Wall

'Hezekiah turned his face to the wall'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו immediately turned to the wall and prayed.

steps.title: What does 'wall' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק means by saying חזקיהו turned to 'the wall.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'wall'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the word 'wall' in the פסוק. This sets up two different answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Why would the פסוק bother telling us he faced a wall? The גמרא assumes the word must teach something deeper about his תפילה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? — introduces a question about meaning

phrases.english: What is meant by 'wall'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and purpose of the word 'קיר' in the פסוק about חזקיהו's prayer.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: He prayed from the walls of his heart
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that 'wall' points to the 'walls of his heart,' meaning חזקיהו prayed with deep, heartfelt sincerity. He proves this from a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: From the walls of his heart. As it is said: 'My insides, my insides, I am in pain; the walls of my heart...'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the first answer: the 'wall' is not a physical wall but the 'walls' of the heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קיר (wall) is read as a hint to קירות לבי (the walls of my heart), a phrase found in ירמיהו. So the פסוק is telling us that חזקיהו's תפילה came from the very depths of his heart.

keyTerms.meaning: The walls (chambers) of his heart — the deepest part of his heart
My insides — an expression of deep inner pain
Etc. — the פסוק continues

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
From the walls of his heart,
as it is said: 'My insides, my insides, I am in pain;'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו ד:יט

phrases.english: the walls of my heart, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: מִקִּירוֹת לִבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'קיר' hints to the walls of the heart: חזקיהו prayed with complete inner sincerity, as in the phrase קירות לבי in ירמיהו.

steps.title: רבי לוי: He mentioned a wall as a merit
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי explains that חזקיהו brought up the topic of a wall. He argued with a קל וחומר: the שונמית built only one small wall for אלישע and her son was brought back to life, so surely ה׳ should save the descendant of שלמה, who covered the whole היכל with silver and gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: It was about matters of a wall. חזקיהו said before ה׳: Master of the World, if the שונמית, who made only one small wall, You brought her son back to life — my father's father, who covered the entire היכל with silver and gold, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives a second, different answer: 'wall' refers to the merit of a wall that חזקיהו used as an argument in his תפילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שונמית built a small walled upper room for אלישע (מלכים ב פרק ד), and in that merit her son was revived. חזקיהו argues with a קל וחומר: if a small wall earned life for her son, then his ancestor שלמה's huge gift of covering the היכל with gold and silver should surely earn life for him. Unlike ריש לקיש, רבי לוי takes 'wall' as an actual wall, used as a merit.

The woman from שונם who built a room for אלישע

steps.title: The words of Hezekiah's prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק with the words of חזקיהו's prayer: remember that I walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and did what was good in Your eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Please remember how I walked before You in truth and with a whole heart, and I did what was good in Your eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the story by quoting the actual words of חזקיהו's prayer from ישעיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his prayer, חזקיהו asks ה׳ to remember his good deeds and sincere service. This fits the idea of praying with merits, as רבי לוי described, and also shows the whole-hearted sincerity that ריש לקיש spoke about.

keyTerms.meaning: Please remember
I walked before You — I served You
With a whole (complete) heart

phrases.english: 'Please remember how I walked before You'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו לח:ג

phrases.english: in truth and with a whole heart,
and I did what was good in Your eyes.'

steps.triggerLanguage: ״זְכָר נָא אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ בֶּאֱמֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story line from step 2 and quotes the words of the prayer. It may also be read as the end of רבי לוי's description of חזקיהו's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו asked ה׳ to remember his sincere and good service.

steps.title: Which good deed did חזקיהו mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what specific good deed חזקיהו meant when he said 'and I did what was good in Your eyes.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'and I did what was good in Your eyes'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on the last words of חזקיהו's prayer and asks which specific deed he meant. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his prayer, חזקיהו already said he walked before ה׳ 'in truth and with a whole heart.' The words 'I did what was good' sound like they point to something more specific. So the גמרא wants to know exactly which deed he had in mind.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by...? (a request to explain a word or phrase)
And I did what was good in Your eyes

phrases.english: What is meant by 'and what was good in Your eyes I did'?
phrases.notes: The quote is from ישעיהו 38:3 and מלכים ב 20:3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks one phrase out of the prayer quoted in step 6 and asks what it refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific good deed חזקיהו was referring to in his prayer.

steps.title: First answer: he joined redemption to prayer
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, says the good deed was that חזקיהו joined גאולה to תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: it means that he joined the blessing of redemption right onto prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer. The good deed was סמיכת גאולה לתפלה, meaning חזקיהו went straight from the ברכה about redemption into his תפלה with no break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גאולה here means the ברכה of גאל ישראל that comes after קריאת שמע. Joining it right onto שמונה עשרה is a praised practice. According to רב, this careful habit was the merit חזקיהו pointed to.

keyTerms.meaning: joined / placed right next to
redemption; here, the ברכה of גאל ישראל after קריאת שמע
prayer; here, the עמידה (שמונה עשרה)

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
That he juxtaposed redemption to prayer.
phrases.notes: He said the ברכה of גאולה and went right into the עמידה with nothing in between.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The good deed was joining גאולה to תפלה.

steps.title: Second answer: he hid away the Book of Remedies
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי says the good deed was that חזקיהו hid away the ספר רפואות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: it means that he hid away the Book of Remedies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives a different answer. The good deed was hiding away the ספר רפואות, a book of cures that people relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People were trusting the book's cures instead of turning to ה׳ in prayer when they were sick. By taking the book out of use, חזקיהו pushed people back toward תפלה. This answer fits well, because חזקיהו himself was sick and praying for healing.

keyTerms.meaning: hid away / put out of use (like storing something in a גניזה)
Book of Remedies, a book of medical cures

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean medicine is bad. The problem was that people relied on this book so much that they stopped humbly praying to ה׳.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
That he suppressed the Book of Remedies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the same question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The good deed was hiding away the ספר רפואות.

steps.title: A ברייתא: six things חזקיהו did
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says חזקיהו did six things. The חכמים agreed with three and did not agree with three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: King חזקיהו did six things. For three of them they agreed with him, and for three of them they did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets up a list of six actions. This line is only the heading. The details come in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא brings this ברייתא here because the first item on its list is hiding the ספר רפואות, the deed רבי לוי just mentioned. It shows that this action really happened and that the חכמים approved of it. The ברייתא also gives a balanced picture: even a great צדיק king made some moves the חכמים disagreed with.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
they agreed with him / approved of what he did

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
King Hezekiah did six things,
with regard to three they agreed with him,
and with regard to three they did not agree with him.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (it backs up רבי לוי's answer)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that mentions רבי לוי's example and widens the discussion to six actions of חזקיהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חזקיהו did six things: the חכמים approved three and did not approve three.

steps.title: The three actions the חכמים agreed with
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים approved of three things: hiding the ספר רפואות, crushing the copper snake, and dragging his father's bones on a bed of ropes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The three they agreed with: He hid away the Book of Remedies, and they agreed with him. He crushed the copper snake, and they agreed with him. He dragged his father's bones on a bed of ropes, and they agreed with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists the three actions the חכמים approved. Each one ends with 'and they agreed with him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hiding the book brought people back to prayer. The נחש הנחשת was the copper snake made by משה in the מדבר, which people had started worshipping, so חזקיהו destroyed it. His father אחז was a wicked king, so חזקיהו gave him a cheap, shameful funeral instead of a royal one, and the חכמים agreed.

keyTerms.meaning: crushed / ground to pieces
the copper snake that משה made (במדבר 21)
dragged
a simple bed made of ropes (not a royal bier)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the snake with the ספר רפואות. They are two separate items. The snake was a real object from משה's time that later became an idol.

phrases.english: With regard to three they agreed with him:
He suppressed the Book of Remedies, and they agreed with him.
He ground the copper snake, and they agreed with him.
phrases.notes: See מלכים ב 18:4. The people were offering incense to it.

phrases.english: He dragged the bones of his father
phrases.notes: His father was the wicked king אחז.

phrases.english: on a bed of ropes, and they agreed with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the heading from step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים approved of hiding the ספר רפואות, crushing the נחש הנחשת, and giving אחז a shameful burial.

steps.title: The three actions the חכמים did not agree with
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים did not approve of three things: stopping up the waters of גיחון, cutting off the היכל doors to send to the king of אשור, and making a leap month in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The three they did not agree with: He stopped up the waters of the Gihon, and they did not agree with him. He cut off the doors of the Sanctuary and sent them to the king of Assyria, and they did not agree with him. He made Nisan a leap month during Nisan, and they did not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list with the three actions the חכמים disapproved. Each one ends with 'and they did not agree with him.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blocking the גיחון spring kept water away from the attacking army, but the חכמים felt he should have trusted ה׳'s promise to protect ירושלים. Stripping the gold off the היכל doors to pay off the Assyrian king took from what was holy. The third item, a leap month made 'in ניסן,' sounds like a plain violation of the תורה. The next two steps raise this problem and explain what חזקיהו really did.

keyTerms.meaning: stopped up / blocked
the waters of the גיחון spring near ירושלים
cut off (the gold of) the doors of the Sanctuary
made a leap year by adding a month

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיהו was a great צדיק, and the חכמים approved several of his bold acts, like hiding the ספר רפואות. Even so, the ברייתא honestly records three moves the חכמים did not approve of.
steps.confusionAlert: 'עבר ניסן בניסן' sounds like adding a second ניסן, which would break a תורה law. Step 14 explains that he actually declared the leap year on the 30th of אדר, a day that might have become ראש חודש ניסן.

phrases.english: He cut off the doors of the Sanctuary

steps.title: How could חזקיהו add an extra ניסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that חזקיהו made a leap month in ניסן. The פסוק teaches that ניסן is the first month and there can be no other ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't חזקיהו accept the פסוק 'This month shall be for you the first of months'? That means: this is ניסן, and no other month can be ניסן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a strong question about step 12. How could a righteous king like חזקיהו do something that seems to go against a פסוק in the תורה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said חזקיהו 'made a leap month in ניסן.' That sounds like he turned a real ניסן into a second אדר. But the פסוק is read to mean that ניסן is fixed and no other month can take its place, so doing that would break a clear תורה law.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't he hold / doesn't he accept? (a challenge formula)
'This month shall be for you' (שמות יב:ב), the source that ניסן is the first month
The first month of the Jewish calendar
Making a leap year by adding an extra month

phrases.english: And does Chizkiyahu not hold (the pasuk):
'This month shall be for you the head of the months':
phrases.notes: שמות יב:ב

phrases.english: this is ניסן, and no other (month) is ניסן?!
phrases.notes: The word 'this' is read as excluding any other month from being ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third disapproved deed listed in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that חזקיהו made a leap month in ניסן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תורה fixes ניסן as the one and only first month. Turning a real ניסן into אדר would be a clear תורה violation, which a righteous king would not commit.

steps.title: He made the leap year on the 30th of אדר
steps.stepSummary: חזקיהו did not break the תורה. He declared the leap year on the 30th of אדר, a day that could have become ראש חודש ניסן. He held that 'since it is fit' is not a reason to forbid this. The חכמים disagreed, as שמואל later taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he made a mistake about the rule that שמואל later taught. שמואל said: we do not make the year a leap year on the 30th day of אדר, because that day is fit to be declared ראש חודש ניסן. חזקיהו held that we do not say 'since it is fit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by redefining what חזקיהו actually did. He did not turn a real ניסן into אדר. He declared the leap year on the last possible day of אדר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 30th day of a month can become ראש חודש of the next month if witnesses see the new moon. So the 30th of אדר is 'fit' to be ניסן, and making it a leap year on that day is too close to touching ניסן. חזקיהו held that a day which only might become ניסן is not ניסן yet, so it is still allowed. The חכמים held it is forbidden. That is why they disapproved.

keyTerms.meaning: He erred regarding the rule taught (later) by שמואל
Make the year a leap year
The 30th day of אדר
'Since it is fit': treating something that could become X as if it were X
We do not say (apply this reasoning)

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל lived many centuries after חזקיהו. 'He erred regarding שמואל' means he erred about the rule that שמואל would later state. It does not mean חזקיהו heard it from שמואל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves חזקיהו from breaking a תורה law. His mistake was only a disagreement over a fine detail of calendar law.

phrases.english: Rather, he erred regarding (the rule of) שמואל
for שמואל said:
We do not make the year a leap year
on the thirtieth day of אדר
since it is fit to be established as (ראש חודש) ניסן.
He (חזקיהו) held: 'since it is fit' — we do not say.
phrases.notes: חזקיהו did not treat a possible ניסן as an actual ניסן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by redefining what חזקיהו actually did.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: it happened on the 30th of אדר, not in a real ניסן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיהו turned a real ניסן into a second אדר, against the pasuk.
steps.terutzMaskana: He declared the leap year on the 30th of אדר. He held that 'הואיל וראוי' does not apply, while the חכמים, like שמואל, held that it does.
steps.whatToRemember: חזקיהו's 'leap month in ניסן' was really a leap year declared on the 30th of אדר. The dispute was whether a day that might become ניסן is treated as ניסן.

steps.title: Relying on your own merit versus the merit of others
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי יוסי בן זמרא, teaches a rule about prayer. Whoever asks based on his own merit is answered because of others' merit. Whoever asks based on others' merit is answered because of his own merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: Whoever relies on his own merit is answered through the merit of others. And whoever relies on the merit of others is answered through his own merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching about how to pray. It connects back to חזקיהו's prayer, where he mentioned his own good deeds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule rewards humility. A person who points to his own merits ends up being helped only because of others. A person who humbly points to others' merits is credited with merit of his own. The next lines of the גמרא use this rule to explain חזקיהו's prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: One who relies on / makes his request depend on
His own merit
The merit of others (for example, the אבות)
It is credited to him / his answer is attributed to

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a lesson about humility in תפלה, which the גמרא will apply to חזקיהו and משה.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
Anyone who relies on his own merit —
they credit him (his answer) through the merit of others.
And anyone who relies on the merit of others —
they credit him through his own merit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the side discussion of חזקיהו's deeds back to the theme of his prayer, by stating a general rule about merit in prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relying on your own merit leads to being answered through others' merit. Relying on others' merit leads to being answered through your own merit.

steps.title: משה relied on the אבות and was credited himself
steps.stepSummary: משה prayed in the merit of אברהם, יצחק and ישראל, and the pasuk in תהלים credits the rescue to משה himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משה relied on the merit of others, as it says: 'Remember אברהם, יצחק and ישראל, Your servants.' And they credited him with his own merit, as it says: 'He said He would destroy them, had not משה His chosen one stood in the breach before Him to turn back His anger from destroying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings משה as proof for the rule in step 15. It shows both halves of the rule from two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the עגל, משה did not mention his own merit. He asked ה׳ to remember the אבות. Yet תהלים describes the rescue as happening because משה himself 'stood in the breach.' This fits exactly: he relied on others and was credited with his own merit.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Remember אברהם' (שמות לב:יג), משה's prayer after the עגל
His chosen one
Stood in the breach, meaning he protected the people
His anger

steps.whatToRemember: משה humbly relied on the אבות, and the pasuk credits him personally. This proves that humility in prayer brings personal merit.

phrases.english: משה relied on the merit of others,
as it says: 'Remember אברהם, יצחק and ישראל, Your servants.'
phrases.notes: שמות לב:יג

as it says: 'He said He would destroy them,'

stood in the breach before Him
to turn back His anger from destroying.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof from פסוקים for the second half of the rule in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that relying on others' merit leads to being credited with your own merit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות לב:יג (משה's prayer) together with תהלים קו:כג (the rescue credited to משה).

steps.title: חזקיהו prayed with his own merit and was answered with others' merit
steps.stepSummary: The first half of רבי יוחנן's rule is proven from חזקיהו. He prayed in his own merit, and הקב״ה answered him in the merit of others: for His own sake and for the sake of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיהו relied on his own merit, as it says: 'Please remember that I walked before You.' So he was answered through the merit of others, as it says: 'I will protect this city to save it, for My sake and for the sake of דוד My servant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the other half of the prayer rule. Someone who asks in his own merit gets answered because of others' merit, and חזקיהו is the example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 showed משה, who asked in others' merit and was credited himself. Now חזקיהו shows the reverse. He said 'remember what I did,' yet הקב״ה's answer mentions only Himself and דוד, not חזקיהו.

keyTerms.meaning: King of יהודה who was sick and prayed for recovery
He based his request on his own merit
Through the merit of others
'And I will protect'
For the sake of דוד, My servant

steps.whatToRemember: משה asked in others' merit and was credited himself. חזקיהו asked in his own merit and was credited to others.

phrases.english: Hezekiah relied on his own merit,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״זְכָר נָא אֵת אֲשֶׁר הִתְהַלַּכְתִּי לְפָנֶיךָ״,

phrases.notes: ישעיהו לח:ג

as it is stated: 'And I will protect this city to save it
phrases.notes: מלכים ב יט:לד

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror-image proof to step 16. It proves the first half of רבי יוחנן's rule (own merit leads to being answered through others' merit).
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who asks in his own merit is answered through others' merit
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו לח:ג (חזקיהו's prayer) together with מלכים ב יט:לד (הקב״ה's answer)

steps.title: Even his good news felt bitter to חזקיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'הנה לשלום מר לי מר' as saying that even when הקב״ה sent חזקיהו peace, it was bitter for him. This fits the idea that he was not answered in his own merit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבי יהושע בן לוי said. רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What does the pasuk mean, 'Behold, for peace I had great bitterness'? Even when הקב״ה sent him peace, it was bitter for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from רבי יהושע בן לוי. He shows that חזקיהו himself felt that something was missing in how he was answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיהו was healed, so why would he feel bitter? According to this reading, it was because his own merit was not counted, just as step 17 said. The pasuk's double 'מר' shows that the bitterness came right alongside the good news.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as / this matches
An early אמורא of ארץ ישראל
'Behold, for peace I had great bitterness'
Sent

steps.confusionAlert: 'שלום' here does not mean a greeting. It means being healed and safe from his illness.

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi taught.
For Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״הִנֵּה לְשָׁלוֹם מָר לִי מָר״ —

phrases.notes: ישעיהו לח:יז

the Holy One, Blessed be He, sent him peace,
it was bitter for him.

steps.raayaObject: That חזקיהו was answered without his own merit being counted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's reading of ישעיהו לח:יז
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that relying on your own merit in prayer can work against you. Humility in תפילה brings a better result.

steps.title: Back to the פסוק about the שונמית's small upper room
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the שונמית's suggestion to build a small walled upper room for אלישע. This sets up a discussion of what that room was.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let us make, please, a small upper room with walls.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of the Shunamite woman and quotes her words. This line sets up the dispute that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here yet. The quote puts the words 'עלית קיר קטנה' on the table so that רב and שמואל can explain what kind of room it was.

keyTerms.meaning: An upper room with a wall
Small
Let us make, please

phrases.english: 'Let us make, please, a small walled upper room.'
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ד:י

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes topic. After finishing the חזקיהו discussion, it returns to the Shunamite woman's story mentioned earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the pasuk 'עלית קיר קטנה' for explanation.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about what the room was
steps.stepSummary: One says there was an open upper floor and they put a roof on it. The other says there was a large porch and they split it in two with a wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One says: there was an open upper floor, and they roofed it. The other says: there was a large enclosed porch, and they divided it into two.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give two different pictures of what the Shunamite woman built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first view, the upper floor already existed and the new work was a ceiling ('קירוה' means they roofed it). In the second view, the room already existed and the new work was a dividing wall.

keyTerms.meaning: One of them said (we are not told which one)
An uncovered, open upper floor
They roofed it over
A large porch or veranda
They divided it into two

steps.confusionAlert: 'קירוה' comes from 'קורה' (a ceiling beam), meaning they put a roof on it. It does not mean they built a wall, even though it sounds like 'קיר'.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel: one said:
It was an uncovered upper floor, and they roofed it.
And one said: It was a large enclosed porch
and they divided it in two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two explanations of the pasuk quoted in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute: either they roofed an open upper floor, or they divided a large porch with a wall.

steps.title: How does the open-upper-floor view explain the word 'wall'?
steps.stepSummary: The porch view fits the word 'קיר', since they built a dividing wall. But the open-upper-floor view only added a roof, so the גמרא asks why the pasuk says 'קיר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says it was a porch, because that is why it says 'wall.' But for the one who says it was an upper floor, what is the 'wall'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the open-upper-floor view, using the word 'קיר' in the פסוק. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dividing a porch requires building a wall, so 'קיר' fits that view perfectly. In the upper-floor view, the new work was a ceiling, not a wall. So the word 'קיר' seems out of place for it.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for (introduces a contrast between two views)
According to the one who says
What is the meaning of 'wall'?

phrases.english: It works well according to the one who said it was a porch,
that explains why 'wall' is written.
But according to the one who said it was an upper floor, what does 'wall' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first opinion of step 20 against the wording quoted in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that it was an open upper floor which they roofed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The pasuk says 'קיר' (wall), but that view has them adding only a ceiling, not a wall.

steps.title: The open-upper-floor view reads 'קיר' as 'they roofed it'
steps.stepSummary: The view that they put a roof on an open upper floor explains the word 'קיר' as coming from 'קירוי,' meaning a roof or ceiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: They roofed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 21. The open-upper-floor view says 'קיר' here does not mean 'wall.' It means they put a ceiling (קירוי) on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that this view has no new wall, so the word 'קיר' seemed out of place. The answer reads 'קיר' as 'roofing,' which is exactly what this view says they did. Now the word fits this opinion too.

keyTerms.meaning: Roofing or a ceiling. The open-upper-floor view reads 'קיר' as coming from this word.
That they roofed it.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'קיר' here as 'wall.' According to this opinion it means 'roof.' That reading is the whole answer.

phrases.english: That they roofed it (put a ceiling on it).
phrases.notes: This is a wordplay: קיר (wall) is read as קירוי (roofing).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 21 against the open-upper-floor view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the pasuk
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'קיר' means wall, so it only fits the porch view.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'קיר' can mean roofing (קירוי), so it fits the open-upper-floor view as well.

steps.title: Challenge to the porch view from the word 'עליית'
steps.stepSummary: The word 'עליית' (upper room) fits the upper-floor view. But for the porch view, which talks about a ground-level porch, why does the pasuk say 'עליית'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who said it was an upper floor, that is why it is written 'עליית' (upper room). But according to the one who said it was a porch, what does 'עליית' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the challenge around. It asks the porch view to explain the word 'עליית,' which seems to mean 'upper floor.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'עליית' naturally means an upper story, which matches the first view perfectly. The porch view says they split an existing porch, so there is no upper floor in that view. The word seems not to fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense. This sets up a contrast where one view fits well and the other has a problem.
An upper floor or upper room.
A porch or veranda.
What does it mean? (Here this is a challenge.)

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who said it was an upper floor,
that is why it is written 'upper room.'
But according to the one who said it was a porch,
what is the meaning of 'upper room'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This mirrors Step 21. That step challenged the upper-floor view; this one challenges the porch view.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'עליית' means an upper story, but the porch view has no upper story.

steps.title: The porch view reads 'עליית' as 'the finest room'
steps.stepSummary: The porch view explains 'עליית' as 'מעולה,' meaning the best or most outstanding of the rooms.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the most outstanding (מעולה) of the rooms.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the porch view. 'עליית' here does not mean 'upstairs.' It means 'the best room.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'עליית' is read as connected to 'מעולה,' which means excellent or superior. So it describes the quality of the room, not its height. With this reading, both words in the pasuk work for both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Excellent, the best.
Of the rooms (of the houses).

steps.whatToRemember: Each opinion reinterprets one word: 'קיר' becomes roofing for the upper-floor view, and 'עליית' becomes 'finest room' for the porch view.

phrases.english: The most outstanding of the rooms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a word in the pasuk
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עליית' means an upper story, so it only fits the upper-floor view.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עליית' can mean 'the finest room' (מעולה), so it fits the porch view as well.

steps.title: The pasuk about the furniture placed in the room
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the rest of the שונמית's words: they will put a bed, table, chair, and lamp in the room for אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And let us place for him there a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the pasuk, about the furniture. This is a setup line that prepares the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of the room itself is finished. Now the גמרא quotes the list of items she planned to put in it. This pasuk will be used for a new teaching in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A bed.
A table.

A lamp or candlestick.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Shunamite woman planned to furnish אלישע's room with a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp.

steps.title: A great person may accept gifts or refuse them
steps.stepSummary: אביי (or רבי יצחק) teaches that a great person who wants to accept gifts may do so, like אלישע. One who does not want to may refuse, like שמואל הרמתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said (some say it was רבי יצחק): Someone who wants to benefit from others may benefit, like אלישע. Someone who does not want to benefit should not benefit, like שמואל from Ramah.
steps.whatsHappening: After the story of the Shunamite woman giving אלישע a room, the גמרא teaches a general rule about whether a great person should accept gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אלישע accepted the room, bed, table, chair, and lamp, so accepting gifts is clearly allowed. שמואל הרמתי took nothing from anyone, so refusing is also a proper path. Both are valid, and each person may choose.

to benefit (from other people's gifts)

steps.title: Proof that שמואל took nothing from others
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says שמואל always returned to Ramah, "for there was his house." רבי יוחנן explains that his house went with him wherever he traveled.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And his return was to Ramah, for there was his house." And רבי יוחנן said: Wherever he went, his house was with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves that שמואל did not accept gifts from people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses "his house" as the reason he kept returning to Ramah. רבי יוחנן reads this to mean that שמואל brought along everything he needed. That way he never had to rely on anyone else's hospitality.

and his return

And Rabbi Yochanan said:

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the פסוקים about the Shunamite woman and draws a lesson from her words to her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is the one who noticed אלישע's holiness and told her husband about it. Her husband did not notice it first. From this, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא learns that women are more perceptive about guests.

from here (we learn)
recognizes, perceives
guests

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman perceives the character of guests better than a man does.

steps.title: How did she know he was holy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא focuses on the words "he is holy" and asks how the שונמית knew this about אלישע.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He is holy": How did she know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to set up the next step: what did she see that showed her אלישע was holy?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holiness is hidden inside a person, so she must have noticed some outward sign. This is a real request for information, not an attack on anyone. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: he is holy
from where did she know?

phrases.english: "He is holy":
How did she know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the word "holy" in the פסוק quoted in step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sign showed the Shunamite woman that אלישע was holy.

steps.title: Two signs of אלישע's holiness
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל give two answers. One says she never saw a fly pass over his table. The other says she spread a white linen sheet on his bed and never found any stain from a nighttime emission on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל disagree. One said: She never saw a fly passing over his table. The other said: She spread a linen sheet on his bed, and she never saw a seminal stain on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing two opinions about what sign she saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first sign is a miracle: even flies stayed away from his table. The second sign shows his purity. White linen shows every mark, and night emissions are common, yet she never found one. The גמרא does not say which of the two אמוראים said which answer.

keyTerms.meaning: one said (one of the two Amoraim)
a fly
a linen sheet
a nighttime seminal emission

steps.confusionAlert: "שמואל" here is the אמורא, the partner of רב. He is not שמואל הרמתי the prophet from step 26.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel (disagree).
phrases.notes: This שמואל is the אמורא, not the prophet.

phrases.english: One said: She never saw a fly
passing over his table,
And the other said: A linen sheet
she spread on his bed,
phrases.notes: White linen shows even small stains.

phrases.english: and she never saw a seminal emission on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Either she never saw a fly over his table, or she never found a stain from a nighttime emission on his white linen sheet.

steps.title: He is holy, but his servant is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא reads "he is holy" as a hint: אלישע himself is holy, but his servant is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He is holy": רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: He is holy, but his servant is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another reading of the same words "he is holy," this time focusing on the word "he."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stressing "he" suggests that only אלישע is holy, and not the person traveling with him. This shows her sharp insight about guests again. She saw through his servant גיחזי as well.

keyTerms.meaning: his servant or attendant (גיחזי)
is not holy

phrases.english: "He is holy":
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
He is holy, but his servant is not holy.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָדוֹשׁ הוּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second lesson from the words "he is holy," which were already discussed in steps 29 and 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words "he is holy" hint that אלישע was holy but his servant גיחזי was not.

steps.title: Proof that גיחזי was not holy
steps.stepSummary: A later פסוק says גיחזי came near to push her away. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that he grabbed her in an immodest way, "by the glory of her beauty."
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "And גיחזי came near to push her away." רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: He grabbed her by the glory of her beauty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the previous step: a later event shows that גיחזי really was not holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word להדפה (to push her) is read as a hint to הוד יפיה (the glory of her beauty). The meaning is that he touched her body in an improper way. This confirms that she judged גיחזי correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: אלישע's servant
to push her away
the glory of her beauty (a modest way of saying her chest)

steps.whatToRemember: The Shunamite woman judged both of her guests correctly. She saw that אלישע was holy and that גיחזי was not. This supports רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's lesson that a woman recognizes guests better than a man.

phrases.english: As it is said: "And Geichazi came near to push her away,"
phrases.notes: מלכים ב ד:כז

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said:
that he grabbed her by the glory of her beauty.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: להדפה is read as הוד יפיה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim of step 31 that the servant was not holy.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק "ויגש גיחזי להדפה", read as "he grabbed her by הוד יפיה".

steps.title: Hosting a Torah scholar is like offering the daily sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: From the words 'עובר עלינו תמיד' (he passes by us continually), רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, teaches that hosting a תלמיד חכם and letting him benefit from your things counts as if you brought the קרבן תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the words 'he passes by us continually (תמיד)': רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: Anyone who hosts a Torah scholar in his home and lets him benefit from his belongings, the פסוק counts it for him as if he were bringing the daily offerings (תמידין).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the Shunamite woman's description of אלישע. It finds a lesson in the word 'תמיד': hosting a Torah scholar is like bringing the daily offerings in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תמיד means 'continually,' but it is also the name of the daily קרבן. The דרשה links the two, so someone who regularly hosts a תלמיד חכם gets credit as if he brought the תמיד. The condition is real hosting: the guest is in your home and benefits from what you own.

keyTerms.meaning: one who hosts a guest
a Torah scholar
lets him benefit from his belongings
the פסוק counts it for him as if
the daily offerings brought every morning and afternoon

steps.whatToRemember: The Shunamite's words about אלישע taught three lessons. A woman can judge guests well. Only אלישע was holy, not גיחזי. And hosting a תלמיד חכם is like bringing the תמיד.

phrases.english: "Passes by us continually"
phrases.notes: The next words of the פסוק in מלכים ב ד, after 'he is holy'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: כָּל הַמְאָרֵחַ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
phrases.english: Anyone who hosts a Torah scholar inside his home
and lets him benefit from his belongings,
the verse credits him
as if he offers the daily offerings.
phrases.notes: A play on the word תמיד: 'continually' and the daily קרבן

steps.triggerLanguage: עוֹבֵר עָלֵינוּ תָּמִיד, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same פסוק and draws a new lesson from them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hosting a תלמיד חכם and providing for him is credited as if one brought the תמיד offerings.

steps.title: Pray from a low place, not a high one
steps.stepSummary: With the same chain of names, the גמרא brings a rule about תפלה: do not stand in a high place to pray. Stand in a low place, as the פסוק says 'ממעמקים קראתיך ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: A person should not stand in a high place and pray. He should pray from a low place, as it says: 'From the depths I called You, ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings another teaching from the same רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא quoting רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. This time it is a practical rule about where to stand when you pray.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic changes from guests to תפלה. The link is the same chain of names. The proof is from תהלים, where the person praying calls to ה׳ 'from the depths.' So the proper place to pray is a low spot, which shows humility.

keyTerms.meaning: a high place
a low place
from the depths
as it says (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practical הלכה that one should not pray while standing on a raised spot.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:

phrases.aramaic: אַל יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם בְּמָקוֹם גָּבוֹהַּ וְיִתְפַּלֵּל,
phrases.english: A person should not stand in a high place and pray;
rather, in a low place, and pray.
As it says: "From the depths I called You, ה׳."
phrases.notes: תהלים קל:א

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, connected only by the same chain of names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should pray from a low place, not a high one, based on 'ממעמקים קראתיך ה׳'.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports praying from a low place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that teaches the same rule in more detail. Do not pray on a chair, a stool, or any high place, because there should be no arrogance before God. It cites ממעמקים and also 'תפלה לעני כי יעטף'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught in a ברייתא: A person should not stand on a chair, or on a stool, or in a high place and pray. He should pray from a low place, because there is no arrogance before God. As it says: 'From the depths I called You, ה׳,' and it is written: 'A prayer of the poor man when he is faint.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the last rule with a ברייתא that says the same thing. The ברייתא also adds examples and the reason behind the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds three things. It gives examples of a high place: a chair or a stool. It states the reason: no arrogance before God. And it adds a second פסוק showing that a person should pray like a poor, humble man.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא also teaches this (a support)
a chair
a stool or footstool
haughtiness, arrogance
a name for God
is faint, overwhelmed

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the word מקום here. In 'מקום גבוה' and 'מקום נמוך' it means a place. But in 'לפני המקום' it is a name for God.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way (in a baraita):

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יַעֲמוֹד אָדָם לֹא עַל גַּבֵּי כִּסֵּא,
phrases.english: A person should not stand, not on top of a chair,
and not on top of a stool,
and not in a high place, and pray;
rather, in a low place, and pray.
Because there is no haughtiness before God.
As it says: "From the depths I called You, ה׳."
And it is written: "A prayer of the poor man when he is faint."
phrases.notes: תהלים קב:א

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 34 with a ברייתא that teaches the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should pray from a low place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing chair, stool, and high place, with the reason 'אין גבהות לפני המקום' and two פסוקים.

steps.title: Line up your feet when you pray
steps.stepSummary: Again in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא teaches that the person praying must line up his feet. The source is the פסוק about the angels: 'ורגליהם רגל ישרה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: One who prays must line up his feet, as it says: 'And their feet were a straight foot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching from the same chain of names. It gives another posture rule for תפלה: keep your feet together and aligned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in יחזקאל describes the angels, whose feet looked like one straight foot. From this we learn that a person praying should stand with his feet together, like the angels. The first posture rule was about where to stand. This one is about how to stand.

keyTerms.meaning: that he align, set in proper position
his feet
a straight foot (the angels' feet looked like one)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two posture rules for תפלה from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Pray from a low place, out of humility. And keep your feet together, like the angels.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the common practice of standing with feet together during שמונה עשרה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
One who prays must align his feet,
as it says: "And their feet were a straight foot."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל א:ז, about the angels

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second posture rule for תפלה from the same chain of names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who prays must place his feet together and aligned, like the angels.

steps.title: Do not eat before praying for your life
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, reads the פסוק 'לא תאכלו על הדם' as a warning not to eat before you pray for your life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said that רבי יוחנן said, and רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: What does the פסוק mean, 'Do not eat on the blood'? It means: do not eat before you have prayed for your blood, that is, for your life.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more teaching from the same chain of names: you may not eat before you pray. It hangs this on a creative reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'על הדם' are read as 'על דמכם.' 'Blood' stands for a person's life, so the פסוק becomes 'do not eat before you pray for your life.' This turns a פסוק about food into a rule about the order of the day: first תפלה, then eating.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (a formula that opens a new reading of a פסוק)
Do not eat 'on the blood' (ויקרא י״ט:כ״ו)
Your blood, meaning your life
Before you pray

steps.confusionAlert: In its simple meaning, the פסוק 'לא תאכלו על הדם' deals with eating meat in connection with blood. It is not about prayer. The prayer meaning here is a דרשה (a teaching built on the words), not the plain meaning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is a source for the well-known הלכה that one should not eat before שחרית.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said
phrases.notes: The parentheses are in the printed text. They show that some versions do not have these words.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
phrases.notes: This is the same chain of names as the earlier teachings in this series.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of what is written, 'You shall not eat on the blood'?
Do not eat before
you have prayed for your blood (your life).
phrases.notes: 'על הדם' is reread as 'על דמכם.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the next teaching in the series of תפלה rules from רבי אליעזר בן יעקב (after not praying from a high place, step 34, and lining up the feet, step 36).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not eat before praying; this is learned from reading 'על הדם' as 'על דמכם.'

steps.title: Second version: eating before praying is arrogance
steps.stepSummary: A second version (איכא דאמרי) of the same teaching says that one who eats and drinks before praying is the person described as casting God 'behind your back,' read as 'behind your pride.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it this way. רבי יצחק said that רבי יוחנן said that רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: Anyone who eats and drinks and only afterward prays, the פסוק says about him: 'And Me you have cast behind your back.' Do not read 'your back' (גויך); read 'your pride' (גאיך). הקב״ה says: Only after this person has puffed himself up did he accept upon himself מלכות שמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another way the same teaching was reported. In this version, eating before praying is described in much stronger words: it is a kind of arrogance toward God.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Version one only says 'do not eat first.' Version two calls the person who eats first someone who puts God behind himself. Using an אל תקרי reading, 'גַּוֶּךָ' (your back) becomes 'גֵּאֶיךָ' (your pride). Taking care of your own needs first, and only then accepting מלכות שמים, means your ego came before God.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say (another version of the same teaching)
And Me you have cast behind your back (מלכים א׳ י״ד:ט׳)
Do not read it as ... but as ... (a reading that changes the vowels to teach a lesson)
Your pride
Became proud or arrogant
The kingdom of Heaven (accepting God as King, as one does in שמע and תפלה)

steps.confusionAlert: איכא דאמרי does not bring a new speaker or a disagreement. It is the same chain of names, reported with a different wording and a sharper message.
steps.whatToRemember: Both versions teach the same practice: pray first, eat afterward. The second version adds why it matters. Eating first puts your own needs, your 'pride,' ahead of accepting מלכות שמים.

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said
that Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Chanina, said
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov:
Anyone who eats and drinks
and only afterward prays,
about him the verse says:
'And Me you have cast behind your back.'
Do not read 'your back,' but rather 'your pride.'
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Only after this one has made himself proud
did he accept upon himself the kingdom of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is an alternate version of the step 37 teaching. It has the same message with a different פסוק and stronger wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who eats and drinks before praying is rebuked as one who puts his own pride ahead of accepting מלכות שמים.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: רבי יהושע's time limit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי יהושע: the morning שמע may be said until three hours into the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי יהושע says, until three hours.
steps.whatsHappening: The long side discussion is over, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה. It quotes רבי יהושע's words to set up the ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything since the earlier discussion of the משנה was a long side trail of אגדה and תפלה teachings, including the חזקיהו story and the שונמית. Now the גמרא picks up the main topic again: the latest time for the morning קריאת שמע. רבי יהושע allows it until the end of the third hour of the day, the time when princes wake up.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהושע says (a quote from the משנה)
Until three hours (into the day)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement by רבי יהושע. It is a quote from the משנה, brought back so the גמרא can comment on it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Until three hours.
phrases.notes: One may say the morning שמע until three hours into the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר עַד שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This leaves the aggadic and תפלה tangent and returns to the משנה about the time of the morning שמע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: (Quoted from the משנה) רבי יהושע: the morning שמע may be said until three hours.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל rules that the הלכה follows רבי יהושע: the morning שמע may be said until three hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling on the time of the morning שמע. We follow רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had more than one view about the deadline for the morning שמע. שמואל settles it in favor of רבי יהושע, so the deadline is three hours into the day. This is the practical bottom line of the discussion about the morning שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of ...
רב יהודה quoting his teacher שמואל

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is that the morning קריאת שמע may be said until the end of three hours into the day, following רבי יהושע.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the basis for the 'סוף זמן קריאת שמע' printed in calendars today.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the practical ruling on the משנה opinion quoted in step 39.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יהושע: the morning שמע may be said until three hours into the day.

steps.title: משנה: one who reads later loses nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one who says שמע after the deadline 'does not lose.' This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One who reads from this time on has not lost.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה. This is a setup line: the next part of the גמרא will explain what 'loses nothing' means and what conditions apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After three hours, a person no longer does the מצוה of שמע at its proper time. Still, he 'does not lose,' because he still gets reward like someone learning תורה (as the ברייתא in step 43 puts it). The גמרא is quoting this line so it can comment on it next.

keyTerms.meaning: From here on (after the three-hour deadline)
He has not lost (he still gets reward, like one learning Torah)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא הפסיד' does not mean he did the מצוה of שמע on time. The מצוה at its set time was missed. He still gains, as a person reading words of תורה.

phrases.english: One who reads from this point onward
has not lost.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This moves to the next phrase of the משנה, after the ruling on רבי יהושע's deadline, to prepare the next comment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: (Quoted from the משנה) One who says שמע after three hours still does not lose; he is rewarded like one reading Torah.

steps.title: He may say שמע late, but not the blessing of יוצר אור
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא, quoting מר עוקבא, limits the משנה: a person who says שמע late 'does not lose' only if he leaves out the ברכות, such as יוצר אור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: This is true only as long as he does not say 'יוצר אור.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains the משנה's words 'does not lose.' After the deadline you may still read שמע, but you should not say its ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכות of the morning שמע, starting with יוצר אור, are tied to the time of the מצוה. Once three hours have passed, רב חסדא holds that those ברכות no longer fit. So the late reader is only like someone reading a section of the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Only as long as / on condition that
'Who forms light,' the first ברכה before the morning שמע
An early אמורא whose teaching רב חסדא passes on

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said:
phrases.notes: Attribution line, merged into this step.

phrases.english: Only as long as he does not say 'Who forms light.'
phrases.notes: This refers to all the ברכות of שמע, starting with the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits the משנה's words 'does not lose,' which were quoted in step 41.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the deadline, one may read שמע but may not say its ברכות.

steps.title: A ברייתא says he does say the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא with a ברייתא saying that a late reader still says two ברכות before שמע and one after.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him from a ברייתא: One who reads from then on does not lose. He is like a person reading from the תורה, but he says two ברכות before it and one after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to say the exact opposite of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees that the late reader is 'like one reading the תורה.' But it adds plainly that he still says the full set of ברכות: two before and one after. That directly clashes with רב חסדא's rule of no יוצר אור.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a תנאי source)
From here on, meaning after the deadline
Two ברכות before שמע and one after it (the morning set)
Like someone reading from the תורה, which is still a מצוה

phrases.english: They raised a challenge:
One who reads from here on does not lose,
like a person who reads from the Torah,
but he does say two blessings before it
and one after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's rule from step 42.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the late reader does not say the ברכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly says that the late reader still says two ברכות before שמע and one after.

steps.title: רב חסדא's view is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the challenge holds. רב חסדא's statement is rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of רב חסדא is a real refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has no answer for רב חסדא, so it declares his view refuted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תיובתא means an אמורא's view cannot stand against a תנאי source. In this version, the late reader does say the ברכות, as the ברייתא taught.

keyTerms.meaning: A conclusive refutation; the view is rejected

steps.whatToRemember: In this first version, רב חסדא's rule of 'no ברכות after the deadline' is rejected. The ברייתא's rule stands: one still says the ברכות.

phrases.english: The refutation of Rav Chisda is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 43 and closes this version.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב חסדא's first version is refuted. A late reader of שמע still says its ברכות.

steps.title: Another version: 'does not lose' means he keeps the blessings
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רב חסדא quoting מר עוקבא says the opposite: 'does not lose' means he does not lose the ברכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב חסדא said in the name of מר עוקבא: What does 'does not lose' mean? That he does not lose the ברכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different report of what רב חסדא said. In this report, he agrees with the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the words 'does not lose' are read as a gain, not a limit. Even after the time for the מצוה of שמע has passed, he may still say the ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say: a second version of the same teaching
What is the meaning of
The blessings said around שמע

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions of רב חסדא say opposite things. The first says no ברכות and is refuted. The second says the ברכות are kept and is supported.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda said that Mar Ukva said:
What does 'does not lose' mean?
That he does not lose the blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the refuted version from step 42 with an opposite report.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Does not lose' in the משנה means that the late reader still says the ברכות.

steps.title: The same ברייתא now supports רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא that refuted the first version now serves as support for the second version.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: One who reads from then on does not lose. He is like a person reading from the תורה, but he says two ברכות before it and one after it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a ברייתא backs up the second version of רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Same words, new job. Before, this ברייתא was used to attack the first version. Now it agrees with the second version, because both say the late reader keeps the ברכות.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a support)

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: one who says שמע after three hours still says two ברכות before it and one after it.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
One who reads from here on does not lose,
like a person who reads from the Torah,
but he does say two blessings before it
and one after it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second version from step 45.
steps.raayaObject: The second version of רב חסדא: the late reader keeps the ברכות
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that the late reader says two ברכות before and one after

steps.title: Saying שמע on time is greater than learning תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני teaches that one who says שמע at its proper time is greater than one who is busy learning תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מני said: One who reads קריאת שמע at its proper time is greater than one who is busy with תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני states a new idea about how valuable it is to say שמע on time. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying שמע on time is compared with learning תורה, and on-time שמע comes out greater. רבי מני will prove this from the משנה's own words.

keyTerms.meaning: At its proper time
One who is busy learning תורה
Greater than

phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said:
Greater is one who reads Shema at its proper time
than one who is busy with Torah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching based on the same line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying שמע on time is greater than learning תורה.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני proves his point. A late reader is only 'like one reading תורה,' so an on-time reader must be greater.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the משנה teaches: 'One who reads from then on does not lose, like a person reading from the תורה,' we learn that one who reads at the proper time is better.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מני brings his proof by reading carefully what the משנה implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The late reader gets the value of learning תורה. The on-time reader must get more than that: learning תורה and also the מצוה of קריאת שמע. So on-time שמע is greater than learning alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Since it teaches (the start of a proof from wording)
By implication, we can infer
Is better / preferred

steps.whatToRemember: A late שמע is worth the same as learning תורה. An on-time שמע is worth more, because it also fulfills the מצוה of קריאת שמע.

phrases.english: Since it teaches:
One who reads from here on does not lose,
like a person who reads from the Torah.
This implies that one who reads at its proper time is better.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רבי מני's claim from step 47.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מני's claim that on-time שמע is greater than learning תורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's comparison of the late reader to 'one reading the תורה'

steps.title: בית שמאי: lie down at night, stand in the morning
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. בית שמאי say a person must lie on his side to say שמע at night and stand to say it in the morning, based on ״וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: At night, every person must lean over on his side and read שמע. In the morning, he must stand. This is because the פסוק says: ״When you lie down and when you rise.״
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new משנה starts here. בית שמאי give their rule for what body position you must be in while saying שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי read the words ״וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ as describing how your body must be positioned. So at night you must actually lie down, and in the morning you must actually stand up. The word 'every person' (כל אדם) means there are no exceptions, even for someone who is already standing or walking.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the opening of a new משנה section)
The school of שמאי's students
He must lean over, meaning lie down on his side
'When you lie down and when you rise' (from the פסוק of שמע)

phrases.english: Mishnah:
phrases.notes: Marks the start of a new משנה.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
In the evening, every person must recline and recite.
phrases.notes: יַטֶּה means leaning over onto one's side.

phrases.english: And in the morning he must stand,
as it is said: 'When you lie down and when you rise.'
phrases.notes: בית שמאי's source. They read it as describing body position.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of the previous one ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, שמע must be said lying down at night and standing in the morning.

steps.title: בית הלל: say it in whatever position you are in
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל disagree. A person may say שמע in any position, because the פסוק also says ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״, which describes someone who is walking.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: Every person reads שמע in his normal way. This is because the פסוק says: ״And when you walk on the road.״
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give the opposite opinion. You may say שמע in whatever position you happen to be in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל point to a different phrase in the same פסוק: ״וּבְלֶכְתְּךָ בַדֶּרֶךְ״. Someone walking on the road is neither lying down nor standing still. This shows that the תורה is not requiring a particular posture.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of הלל's students
In his normal way, meaning however he happens to be
'And when you walk on the road'

steps.confusionAlert: 'כדרכו' does not mean 'on his journey.' It means 'in his usual manner,' whatever position he is already in.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
Every person recites in his own manner.
phrases.notes: Any position is acceptable.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'And when you walk on the way.'
phrases.notes: A walking person is neither lying down nor standing still.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, שמע may be said in any position.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'lie down' and 'rise'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks a question on בית הלל: if posture does not matter, what do the words ״וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ come to teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say ״When you lie down and when you rise״?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question on בית הלל's view. This sets up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית הלל are right that position does not matter, the words 'lie down' and 'rise' seem to have no job. The משנה needs to show what these words do teach according to בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your view is correct)
Why was it said? (what does this phrase teach?)

phrases.english: If so, why is it said:
'When you lie down and when you rise'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how בית הלל explain the פסוק that בית שמאי rely on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words ״וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ teach, according to בית הלל.

steps.title: The words describe the time, not the position
steps.stepSummary: Answer: ״וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ tells us WHEN to say שמע. It means at the time people go to sleep and at the time people get up.
steps.simpleTranslation: At the time when people lie down, and at the time when people get up.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question for בית הלל. The words 'lie down' and 'rise' are telling us the time of שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית הלל, the פסוק is giving a time frame: the hours when people normally go to bed and the hours when people normally wake up. Read this way, the phrase is not wasted, and it fits with the earlier discussion about the times of שמע.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time when
Lie down (go to sleep)
Get up (from sleep)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the הלכה that שמע has fixed times, night and morning, while the body position does not matter.

phrases.english: At the time when people lie down
and at the time when people rise.
phrases.notes: The phrase describes time, not posture.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 51.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״וּבְשָׁכְבְּךָ וּבְקוּמֶךָ״ refers to the time when people sleep and wake up, not to body position.

steps.title: רבי טרפון reclined on the road and was endangered
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון tells that he was traveling and lay down to say שמע the way בית שמאי require. In doing so, he put himself in danger from bandits.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: I was traveling on the road, and I lay down to read שמע the way בית שמאי say. I put myself in danger because of the bandits.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי טרפון tells a personal story. He followed בית שמאי's rule and ended up in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון followed בית הלל, but he tried to be extra careful by also doing what בית שמאי require. Lying down on a road where bandits attack travelers put his life at risk. The story warns against acting like בית שמאי when the הלכה follows בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who was a student of בית הלל
I leaned over (lay down)
I put myself in danger
Bandits, highway robbers

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows בית הלל: שמע may be said in any position. The words 'lie down' and 'rise' set the times for saying it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon said:
I was coming along the road
and I reclined to recite according to the words of Beit Shammai.
And I endangered myself because of the bandits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן: אֲנִי הָיִיתִי בָּא בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story about following בית שמאי's opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lying down on the road to follow בית שמאי led to danger from bandits.

steps.title: The Sages tell רבי טרפון he deserved the danger for going against בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The Sages respond to רבי טרפון: you deserved to be in danger, because you went against the words of בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: You deserved to be liable with your own life, because you went against the words of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The Sages answer רבי טרפון's story. They say the danger he faced was deserved, because he acted against בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows בית הלל, who allow saying שמע in any position. רבי טרפון chose to be extra strict like בית שמאי and lay down on the road. The Sages say that going against בית הלל this way is not praiseworthy extra piety. It is a real wrongdoing, so the danger was fitting.

keyTerms.meaning: Worthy of / deserving
To be liable with your own self (your life)
You transgressed / went against
The words (ruling) of בית הלל

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows בית הלל: שמע may be said in any position. Being 'extra strict' like בית שמאי, against בית הלל, is treated as going against the הלכה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי טרפון was praised for being extra careful. The Sages criticize him. Choosing בית שמאי's stricter view over בית הלל is considered going against the ruling, not a bonus מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important principle: once the הלכה is set like בית הלל, following בית שמאי, even to be strict, is a problem. The גמרא will soon explain why this is so serious.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: The Sages are answering רבי טרפון.

phrases.english: You deserved to be liable with your own life,
phrases.notes: The danger from the bandits was fitting.

phrases.english: because you went against the words of בית הלל.
phrases.notes: The reason: the הלכה follows בית הלל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: כְּדַי הָיִיתָ לָחוּב בְּעַצְמְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds directly to רבי טרפון's story in step 53. It judges his choice to follow בית שמאי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going against בית הלל, even to be strict like בית שמאי, is a wrongdoing serious enough that one deserves the resulting danger.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows בית הלל on the posture for saying שמע. Deliberately following בית שמאי instead is condemned, not praised.
